units.translation: It was written τεράζων [portending]. For it had not been noticed that in M, in the text and in the lemma of the scholium, τεράιζων [portending] is written, as in Photius Lex. p. 577, 16. τεραΐζεισ [you portend] is in the codex. For τεράζω [I portend] has the iota written beneath, as Etym. M. p. 737, 21 and the grammarian in Cramer's Anecd. Oxon. vol. 1 p. 226 point out. The same is the spelling of other verbs of this kind, such as ματάζω [I act in vain] and σφαδάζω [I struggle], which were written without the iota in Aeschylus Agam. 995, Pers. 194, Soph. Oed. R. 891. Herodian gave accurate instructions about all these in his book περὶ μονήρους λέξεως [on the anomalous word] p. 23, 7. But wrongly γυμνάιζεται [he exercises] M Pr. 592.
Thus he spoke, portending.
